item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Srettha Thavisin’s 2024 record on 7B.9 is mixed but leans negative. The clearest negative evidence is the Pichit Chuenban cabinet appointment and the ethics dismissal that followed. The clearest positives are one technocratic cabinet pick, public asset disclosure, and some remaining room for press criticism. I did not find reliable Srettha-specific 2024 evidence on pardons or procurement; the strongest signal comes from appointments and information access.

**Accepted Claims**
- `Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge` | Reuters | 2024-04-28 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984) | Claim: Srettha named Pichai Chunhavajira, a former SET chair and Bank of Thailand board member, as finance minister and deputy PM. That is a real technocratic counter-signal to pure patronage in top economic staffing. IDs: `7B.9`
- `Srettha and his wife worth B1bn` | Bangkok Post | 2024-06-17 | [URL](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2812379/declaration) | Claim: Srettha publicly declared assets and liabilities to the NACC, which shows some willingness to operate under external financial scrutiny. IDs: `7B.9`
- `Thailand` | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | [URL](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand) | Claim: Thai media could still criticize government policy and cover corruption, but self-censorship, lèse-majesté constraints, and backroom coalition deals kept accountability weak. This is mixed evidence on access to public information. IDs: `7B.9`
- `Thai court dismisses PM Thavisin for gross ethics violation` | EFE | 2024-08-14 | [URL](https://efe.com/en/latest-news/2024-08-14/thai-court-dismisses-pm-over-ethics-case/) | Claim: the Constitutional Court removed Srettha over the Pichit Chuenban appointment, where Pichit had a prior bribery-related conviction. This is the strongest evidence for ethically compromised, network-based appointment politics. IDs: `7B.9`
- `Thai journalists arrested for news coverage of anarchist graffiti on temple` | Reuters via Yahoo News | 2024-02-13 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thai-journalists-arrested-news-coverage-054141721.html) | Claim: the arrest of two journalists for reporting on anti-royal graffiti created a chilling effect on scrutiny and public information access under Srettha’s government. IDs: `7B.9`
- `Thailand's $13.5 billion household stimulus plan gets cabinet approval` | Reuters | 2024-04-23 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Claim: the 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million people was Pheu Thai’s signature, highly visible distributive program. It is relevant as transactional/populist politics, though it is not proof of illegal clientelism by itself. IDs: `7B.9`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a reliable 2024 Srettha-specific source on pardons or procurement that clearly showed either favoritism or clean neutrality.
- The evidence base is concentrated in cabinet appointments, press freedom, and one large distributive policy.
